statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42014 (GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-9): changing the Security Officer PIN with gnutls_pkcs11_token_set_pin() with oldpin set to NULL, for a PKCS#11 token that lacks a protected authentication path, used the token URI after it had been freed (lib/pkcs11_write.c). It was reported as https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1766 . GnuTLS fixed it in 3.8.13 with commit 3957f136e2ed23caf176a594b54b3827f5cef701 (pkcs11_write: fix UAF and leak in gnutls_pkcs11_token_set_pin), which moves the p11_kit_uri_free() call from straight after the session is opened to the error path and the common exit: https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/3957f136e2ed23caf176a594b54b3827f5cef701, https://gnutls.org/security-new.html, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/blob/3.8.13/NEWS . Alpine's 3.23-stable gnutls APKBUILD builds gnutls from the upstream release and lists CVE-2026-42014 under its 3.8.13-r0 security fixes: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/gnutls/APKBUILD . We downloaded every package built from the gnutls source in the Alpine 3.23 main index of the DHI Alpine repository as listed on 2026-11-28: gnutls, gnutls-c++, gnutls-dbg, gnutls-dev, gnutls-doc and gnutls-utils, each at 3.8.11-r0, 3.8.12-r0, 3.8.13-r0 and 3.8.14-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64, 48 apks, and checked each download against its index checksum. The library code is in libgnutls.so.30 in the gnutls package, a dynamically linked shared library whose needed libraries include musl's C library and libp11-kit.so.0, so PKCS#11 support is built in. gnutls-c++ ships the C++ wrapper libgnutlsxx.so.30, which links libgnutls.so.30; gnutls-utils ships seven programs (certtool, gnutls-cli, gnutls-cli-debug, gnutls-serv, ocsptool, p11tool and psktool), each dynamically linked against libgnutls.so.30 and loaded by the musl dynamic loader; gnutls-dev ships headers, gnutls.pc and the libgnutls.so and libgnutlsxx.so symbolic links; gnutls-doc ships man pages, info manuals and text documentation; gnutls-dbg ships separate debug-symbol files for the two libraries and the seven programs. None of the 48 packages contains a static archive, a PE file or a Mach-O file. The GnuTLS version string in libgnutls.so.30 reads 3.8.11, 3.8.12, 3.8.13 and 3.8.14 in the matching builds on both architectures. We disassembled gnutls_pkcs11_token_set_pin in libgnutls.so.30 of every build, locating it with the gnutls-dbg symbols: the 3.8.11-r0 and 3.8.12-r0 builds call p11_kit_uri_free once, as the unfixed source does, and the 3.8.13-r0 and 3.8.14-r0 builds call it twice, as the fixed source does, on both architectures. So 3.8.11-r0 and 3.8.12-r0 are affected and 3.8.13-r0 is the first fixed build; 3.8.14-r0 also carries the fix.

CVE-2026-42014: gnutls_pkcs11_token_set_pin, used to change a PKCS#11 token's Security Officer PIN, could use memory after freeing it when called with a NULL old PIN for a token without a protected authentication path. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-9 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-9, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1766) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/3957f136e2ed23caf176a594b54b3827f5cef701. Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42014), which applies the 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version; the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 records this CVE. The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources sort below it and are reported as affected.
